<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * Local inline 16px split-header glyphs, sibling of RowGlyph (no icon font,
 * no CDN). Purely decorative: every glyph is aria-hidden and its button
 * carries the accessible name in visually hidden text.
 */
defineProps<{
  name: 'menu' | 'search' | 'commands' | 'star' | 'back' | 'reminders';
  /** Star only: a filled star for the pressed (filter on) state. */
  filled?: boolean;
}>();
</script>

<template>
  <svg
    class="header-glyph-icon"
    width="16"
    height="16"
    viewBox="0 0 16 16"
    fill="none"
    stroke="currentColor"
    stroke-width="1.4"
    stroke-linecap="round"
    stroke-linejoin="round"
    aria-hidden="true"
    focusable="false"
  >
    <!-- Destinations: the hamburger. -->
    <path v-if="name === 'menu'" d="M2.75 4.25h10.5M2.75 8h10.5M2.75 11.75h10.5" />
    <!-- Find mail: a magnifier. -->
    <template v-else-if="name === 'search'">
      <circle cx="7" cy="7" r="4.25" />
      <path d="M10.25 10.25l3 3" />
    </template>
    <!-- Commands: the command-key loop. -->
    <path
      v-else-if="name === 'commands'"
      d="M10 4v8a2 2 0 1 0 2-2H4a2 2 0 1 0 2 2V4a2 2 0 1 0-2 2h8a2 2 0 1 0-2-2"
    />
    <!-- Starred only filter: outline at rest, filled while the filter is on. -->
    <path
      v-else-if="name === 'star'"
      d="M8 2.4l1.7 3.5 3.85.55-2.8 2.7.67 3.85L8 11.2 4.58 13l.67-3.85-2.8-2.7 3.85-.55z"
      :fill="filled ? 'currentColor' : 'none'"
    />
    <!-- Back to previous context: a left arrow. -->
    <template v-else-if="name === 'back'">
      <path d="M7 3.75L2.75 8 7 12.25" />
      <path d="M3 8h10.25" />
    </template>
    <!-- Local reminders: a clock. -->
    <template v-else>
      <circle cx="8" cy="8" r="5.25" />
      <path d="M8 5.25V8l1.9 1.4" />
    </template>
  </svg>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * Gmail mailbox shell: compact browsing shell (UX-01), plain-text reader,
 * operation recovery, and explicit account/action capability gates.
 *
 * Account gate: the account status read decides fixture-vs-Gmail. While the status
 * is loading or failed, the UI renders no mailbox content at all — it never falls
 * back silently to fixture mode.
 *
 * Layout contract: a persistent narrow email rail, a compact Inbox
 * navigation/status header, one central surface that is either the list or the
 * reader (never both), and contact context. Account/Activity/Drafts live in
 * explicit labelled utility disclosures instead of permanent competing columns;
 * the contact pane shows only exact known fields.
 *
 * Keyboard contract (window-level, one handler):
 * - j / ArrowDown, k / ArrowUp: move conversation focus in the list (row focus
 *   follows). Inside the reader only j/k switch conversations; ArrowUp/Down
 *   keep native scrolling there.
 * - Enter: open the focused conversation. Escape: close the active utility or
 *   contact disclosure first, then the reader.
 * - e: archive the focused (or reader-open) conversation when actions are enabled.
 * - Shift+E: restore to Inbox; G then E (within 1000ms): cached Done.
 * - Left from list navigation: destination navigator; pointer Commands opens palette.
 * - Cmd+K opens the palette in native mode only (browser reservations stay native).
 * - Shift+U: explicitly mark the focused/open conversation unread.
 * - z: undo the last accepted conversation action (single level, 10 s window;
 *   the backend's eligibility decision is authoritative). Cmd/Ctrl+Z is left
 *   to native text editing.
 * - Ignored with Ctrl/Meta/Alt held, during IME composition, inside text fields, and
 *   Enter/e are ignored when a button owns the key (it activates itself).
 * - While a visible draft editor exists, every mailbox shortcut is suppressed;
 *   a suspended editor behind another disclosure must not own keys. While a
 *   utility/contact disclosure is open, Escape closes it and mailbox shortcuts
 *   underneath are suppressed. Draft text has no submit/send path and is
 *   rendered only as ordinary text.
 */
import { computed, nextTick, onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref, watch } from 'vue';
import CachedTrashPanel from './components/CachedTrashPanel.vue';
import { emptyCachedTrash } from './lib/cached-trash';

content.text:
The header pass is done. The app header is now a single 78px borderless strip inside the list column; it was 144px in Gmail mode and 115px in fixture mode. `pnpm typecheck` is clean and `pnpm test` passes 635 tests, with 32 skipped and no failures. Nothing is committed or pushed, and the rows pass is unchanged.

**Height (measured in Chromium)**
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Gmail mode, 1030 and 1280 | 144px full-width, first list item at y=144 | 78px in the list column, first list item at y=78 |
| Fixture workspaces (dev page) | 115px | 78px |

**Files changed**
- `src/App.vue`: new header markup. The header and the in-flow notices moved inside `<main>`, so they share its overlay inertness and the list column's grid track. The rail and contact pane now run to the top of the window. I removed the unused `pendingCount` and added a few computeds for the tabs, coverage and starred filter.
- `src/components/HeaderGlyph.vue` (new): a sibling of `RowGlyph`, with local inline SVG for menu, search, commands, star (outline or filled), back and reminders.
- `src/assets/style.css`: new header and tab styles, and new `--text-tertiary`, `--icon-muted` and `--split-header-height` tokens. It also deletes the old styles for the brand text, banner, status line and violet chip tabs.
- `tests/discovery.rendered.test.ts`: one intended change. The hamburger is now the first header Tab stop, so the test reaches Destinations with Shift+Tab from Commands.
- `DESIGN.md`: Parity Gaps item 1 rewritten as done, with what remains.

**Every removed or moved header element**
| Element | Where it went |
|---|---|
| "Email" brand | Deleted |
| "Inbox"/context h1 | Still in the accessibility tree and tests (`inbox-title`). On screen only when no tab is active (Cached Done, Starred, Search, reader, open drawer), styled like an active tab. |
| Destinations chip | Hamburger glyph, which opens the navigator; Left from the list also opens it. |
| Commands chip | Glyph on the right; Cmd+K in the native app. |
| Search chip | Glyph on the right; `/` still works. |
| Starred only (cached) chip | Star glyph toggle that shows its pressed state, plus a "Starred only" tag in words beside the tabs (filter state in words, not just a tint). I didn't use a tab, because tabs are navigation and this filters the current view. I didn't use the hamburger, because the navigator lists destinations. |
| Reminders chip (fixture only) | Clock glyph, still named "Reminders"; G then H and the navigator also work. |
| Remind me chip | Removed. It acts on one conversation and is reachable with H and in the palette. |
| Back to previous context chip | Back-arrow glyph, shown only when there is history. |
| Split tab chip | Borderless tabs: active white-ish, inactive muted, 11px count 4px after. The violet treatment is gone. |
| Coverage sentence | Accessible description of each tab plus a hover title on the tab strip. The sentence qualifies the counts, so it now sits on them. Gmail only, as before. |
| Browser-preview banner | One-line amber "Preview · in-memory" note on the right. The full disclosure is its title and screen-reader text. Browser preview only. |
| "Saved split unavailable" alert | Still in the header, as a row under the tab line. |

**What each status-line fact became**
| Fact | Outcome |
|---|---|
| "18 in inbox" / "loaded in …" / "search results loaded" | Dropped. The inbox count is on the active tab, the Done and Search coverage notes already report totals or "unknown", and loaded counts repeat the list. |
| "Gmail is read-only · Review access in Account" | Kept as a short note with its button on the right. It is the only visible explanation for why actions are missing. |
| "Unread only" | Kept as a visible filter tag beside the tabs, same live-region role. |
| "N selected" | Shown in the SelectionBar; the announcement is kept in a visually hidden polite live region. |
| "N pending operation(s)" | Dropped as a duplicate of the row's "Pending…", the action notice and Activity. |
| "Shift+U marks…" | Dropped; the Commands palette lists Mark unread with Shift+U. |
| "last command failed: …" | Moved to its own alert line next to the action notice (above the list). I kept it out of the action notice's polite region so it is announced once. It still shows in Cached Trash, where the action notice is hidden. |

**Regression found and fixed:** once the glyphs moved right, an open utility drawer covered the Commands glyph. In browser preview that is the only pointer route to the palette. Drawers now start below the header.

**Verification**
- I also ran the real-Chromium test suites, which are normally skipped. Discovery passes 16/16. 30 passed and 1 skipped overall.
- One failure is pre-existing: "archives with action-time neighbor ordering after a mid-reading list reorder" in `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts` times out at 5s. It fails the same way on a clean checkout of HEAD.
- In Chromium I exercised the hamburger, Left from the list, Commands, Cmd+K (native), search, the starred toggle and Back, switching tabs, Cached Done, the split editor, the drawer and selection.
- Tab order is: hamburger, tabs, (Review access), star, Commands, Search, then the rail.
- Vite is stopped, the headless browser is closed, and the temporary baseline worktree is removed.

**Deliberately not done**
- **Compose glyph:** not added. The only compose-like capability is local drafts in the Drafts drawer, and a header compose button would overstate that. Whether "New local draft" earns the slot is your call.
- **Out of scope:** the rows, rail, contact pane, action notice and SelectionBar styling, the Done/Starred coverage note styling (still at a 1rem inset) and type sizes outside the header.

**Remaining gaps**
- The total pending count has no glanceable home outside Activity; a badge on the rail's Activity button in the rail pass would fix that.
- The tab line should be lined up with the rail's top button once the 40px rail ships.
- With a drawer open, the top of the contact pane shows above the drawer's edge.
